title: Excessive disclosure during registration and device enrollment
description: The homeowner may be required or nudged to provide more personal data than is necessary to create the account or enroll cameras/sensors, such as unnecessary profile details, household composition, or precise location information.
assumptions: Registration/enrollment may collect identity, contact, device identifiers, and home/location-related data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for a disclosure/minimisation-related source-side threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Linkability via persistent identifiers in transit
description: Account registration and device enrollment data may include persistent identifiers such as email address, account ID, serial numbers, MAC addresses, or installation identifiers that allow records and actions to be linked to the same household or person across sessions or systems.
assumptions: The flow carries account attributes and device identifiers needed for enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from identifiers on the data flow; exact subtree numbering may vary.

title: Identifiability of homeowner from registration data
description: Personally identifying data in the registration flow, such as name, email, phone number, address, or precise home location, can directly identify the homeowner or household when transmitted to the Home Hub.
assumptions: The registration step includes direct identifiers or highly identifying combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability due to direct identifiers in the flow; exact numbering may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive household and device metadata in transit
description: Enrollment traffic may reveal sensitive information about the home environment, including number and type of cameras/sensors, room placement hints, network identifiers, and timing of setup, which could expose security posture or occupancy-related details if observed in transit.
assumptions: The flow contains device model/type, identifiers, and setup metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of content/metadata on the flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Linkability through centralized account and device association
description: On receipt, the Home Hub can associate the homeowner account with all enrolled cameras and sensors, creating a consolidated profile of the household and enabling linkage of future events and device activity to the same person or home.
assumptions: The Home Hub stores account-to-device mappings for management and operation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side linkage through stored associations; exact numbering may differ.

title: Identification of household through stored enrollment records
description: The Home Hub may store registration and enrollment records in a way that makes the homeowner or household directly identifiable, for example by retaining names, contact details, address, and device ownership together.
assumptions: The Home Hub persists account and device enrollment data locally or forwards it for persistence.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side identifiability from stored personal data; exact numbering may differ.

title: Over-retention and secondary use of registration/enrollment data
description: The Home Hub may retain account and device enrollment data longer than necessary or reuse it for analytics, diagnostics, profiling, or feature development beyond what the homeowner expects from setup.
assumptions: The destination stores setup data and may support telemetry, analytics, or later administrative uses.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side disclosure through retention/secondary use; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency about enrollment data processing
description: The homeowner may not be adequately informed about what personal and device data the Home Hub collects during registration/enrollment, why it is needed, how long it is stored, and with whom it is shared.
assumptions: Privacy notices or setup UX may be incomplete or hard to understand.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness/lack of transparency; exact numbering may differ.

title: Processing without valid or sufficiently specific consent/legal basis
description: If the Home Hub collects optional personal data or uses enrollment data for non-essential purposes without obtaining valid consent or another appropriate legal basis, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Some collected data or downstream uses may be optional or not strictly necessary for core enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to legal basis/consent; exact numbering may differ.

title: Lack of evidence of homeowner choices during registration
description: The system may fail to record the homeowner's privacy choices, notices presented, or consent/preferences selected during account creation and device enrollment, making later disputes about what was agreed difficult to resolve.
assumptions: The setup process includes privacy-relevant choices or acknowledgements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation-related privacy threat; exact numbering may differ.

title: Interception of temporary access code in transit
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest may be observed or captured while being transmitted from the guest-facing input path to the Home Hub logic, revealing the guest's credential and enabling identification of the guest's visit or misuse of the code.
assumptions: Assumes the code traverses a communicable path or interface where eavesdropping, shoulder-surfing of an attached interface, or interception is possible beyond purely local ephemeral entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for confidentiality/interception of authentication secrets may differ.

title: Linking guest visits through repeated code use or event records
description: If the Home Hub stores or correlates temporary access codes, timestamps, and unlock events, it may link multiple door-access events to the same guest or household interaction pattern, allowing reconstruction of visit histories.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub logs code identifiers or stable metadata across multiple accesses.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via stored identifiers and event correlation.

title: Identification of guest from access code and access event
description: The Home Hub may be able to associate the temporary access code and time of use with a specific invited guest, thereby identifying who accessed the home at a particular time.
assumptions: Assumes temporary codes are uniquely assigned per guest or can be mapped to a guest by the homeowner or service.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact identification subtree node may vary.

title: Disclosure of guest presence and visit timing
description: Processing or storing the entered code and unlock result at the Home Hub can disclose sensitive information about the guest's presence at the residence, arrival time, and potentially behavioral patterns if logs are retained or shared.
assumptions: Assumes access attempts or successful unlocks are logged, displayed, or made available to other parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ depending on whether disclosure is internal, external, or via logging.

title: Guest cannot plausibly deny code entry or door access
description: If the Home Hub records the temporary code use with timestamps, the resulting audit trail may prevent the guest from plausibly denying that they attempted or performed the unlock action, which can create privacy concerns around traceability of their actions.
assumptions: Assumes logs are retained and treated as evidence of the guest's action.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation as a privacy threat; exact subtree node uncertain.

title: Guest may be unaware of logging and secondary use of access events
description: The guest may not be informed that entering the temporary access code causes the Home Hub to log access attempts, retain timestamps, or share notifications with the homeowner or third parties, reducing transparency about processing.
assumptions: Assumes no clear notice is provided at the point of code entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node id; exact transparency-related subtree may differ.

title: Use of guest access data beyond the expected purpose
description: The Home Hub may process or retain the temporary code and associated access event for purposes beyond immediate door unlocking, such as long-term monitoring, analytics, or sharing with other systems, without a privacy-compatible justification.
assumptions: Assumes secondary use, excessive retention, or sharing occurs beyond what the guest reasonably expects for entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact node depends on the applicable policy or legal requirement.

title: Sensor event records enable linkage of household activity over time
description: By writing motion, door, and other sensor events into a persistent local log, the Home Hub creates a longitudinal record that can be linked across time to infer routines, occupancy patterns, and relationships between events originating from the same home or occupants.
assumptions: The local event log stores multiple events over time with timestamps or stable device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Event contents may identify occupants or devices
description: The Home Hub may write event details such as device IDs, room names, sensor labels, or precise timestamps that allow identification of a specific household, room, or person associated with the events.
assumptions: Logged events include identifiers, labels, or sufficiently distinctive metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat applicability depends on event schema.

title: Local event log reveals sensitive household behavior
description: Once stored in the Local Event Log, the event history can disclose sensitive information such as presence at home, sleep/wake cycles, movement patterns, and periods of absence, exposing private behavior to anyone with access to the datastore.
assumptions: The datastore retains readable event history and can be accessed by local users, admins, malware, or forensic tools.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact disclosure subtree may differ.

title: Stored event history enables detection of habits and occupancy
description: Analysis of the accumulated log allows detection of regular routines, occupancy schedules, and unusual deviations, even if individual events seem innocuous in isolation.
assumptions: Events are timestamped and retained long enough for pattern analysis.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate.

title: Logging may occur without sufficient user awareness or control
description: Users may be unaware that detailed motion and door events are being persistently stored locally, for how long, and for what purposes, reducing their ability to make informed privacy choices.
assumptions: The system does not clearly notify users about local logging behavior, retention, or controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree may differ.

title: Persistent local logging may exceed user expectations or consent
description: If the Local Event Log stores more event detail or retains it longer than users expect or agreed to, the processing may be non-compliant with stated purposes, minimization, or retention commitments.
assumptions: There are privacy expectations, policies, or consent choices that may not align with actual logging scope or retention.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because compliance-related subtrees vary by catalog version.

title: Local logs may be used as evidence of occupant actions without adequate contestability
description: The stored event log can later be treated as proof that someone entered, moved, or was present, while occupants may have limited ability to challenge the accuracy, context, or completeness of those records.
assumptions: Logs are relied upon for troubleshooting, monitoring, or disputes and may be considered authoritative.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is somewhat context-dependent; node id is best-fit from memory.

title: Excessive disclosure of household video content to cloud storage
description: The Home Hub uploads recorded camera clips containing occupants, visitors, interiors, routines, and potentially audio/other sensitive contextual data to the cloud. Sending full clips rather than minimized or filtered content can disclose more personal data than necessary for the storage purpose.
assumptions: Recorded clips may contain identifiable people, private spaces, timestamps, and contextual details; upload may include full-resolution footage and metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Linkability via upload metadata and persistent identifiers in transit
description: Even if clip payloads are protected, the flow may expose stable device/account identifiers, IP addresses, timing, clip IDs, and upload patterns that allow an observer or intermediary to link multiple uploads to the same household, device, or user over time.
assumptions: Network-visible metadata or protocol headers reveal persistent identifiers or consistent traffic patterns.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; threat applicability depends on transport protections and metadata exposure.

title: Identifiability of residents from video and transport metadata
description: The uploaded clips themselves may directly identify residents, visitors, or neighbors through faces, voices, home interiors, or unique possessions. In-transit metadata such as source IP/geolocation and account-linked identifiers can further identify the household behind the uploads.
assumptions: Clips contain recognizable individuals or uniquely identifying household context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Linking stored clips across time and services at cloud storage
description: Cloud Video Storage can correlate uploaded clips over time using account IDs, device IDs, timestamps, and household identifiers, building a longitudinal picture of occupancy, routines, visitors, and events. If combined with other cloud datasets, this increases cross-context linkability.
assumptions: The cloud service stores uploads under persistent account/device identifiers and may have access to other service data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; exact subtree for recipient-side linking may differ.

title: Identification of household members by cloud-side analysis
description: The destination may use the received clips and metadata to identify specific individuals or households, for example through facial recognition, voice recognition, address/account association, or inference from interior scenes and timestamps.
assumptions: Cloud storage or associated services can analyze content and associate it with subscriber identity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact node id may differ.

title: Secondary use or over-retention of uploaded video at the destination
description: Once clips reach cloud storage, the service may retain them longer than expected or process them for analytics, model training, law-enforcement response workflows, or product improvement beyond the user's immediate storage purpose, disclosing personal information to additional parties or purposes.
assumptions: Service terms or backend operations may permit retention, internal access, or onward sharing beyond simple storage.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this combines recipient-side disclosure and purpose expansion concerns.

title: Unawareness of cloud upload, retention, and downstream processing
description: Residents, visitors, or even the subscribing user may not be fully aware that clips are uploaded to cloud storage, how long they are retained, who can access them, or whether they are analyzed or shared onward. This undermines informed expectations about the processing.
assumptions: Not all data subjects receive clear notice about cloud storage and downstream processing of recordings.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact unawareness subtree may differ.

title: Insufficient ability to exercise control over uploaded clips
description: After upload, users or recorded individuals may lack effective means to delete clips promptly, restrict sharing, disable certain analyses, manage retention, or object to processing. This creates non-compliance risk with data subject rights and user control expectations.
assumptions: Cloud storage may not provide granular controls for deletion, retention, access restriction, or objection to secondary processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact non-compliance/control-related node may differ.

title: Repudiation gaps around upload and access events
description: If the cloud service does not maintain trustworthy records of when clips were uploaded, accessed, shared, or deleted, parties may later be unable to prove or dispute whether specific personal video data was processed. This can hinder accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Auditability and evidence of processing events may be incomplete or not exposed to users.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; repudiation is less central here than other threats.

title: Motion alert content reveals occupant activity to the backend
description: By forwarding a real-time motion alert, the Home Hub discloses that motion was detected at a specific home and time. This can reveal presence, routines, or occupancy patterns of residents to the backend operator.
assumptions: The alert is associated with a household, device, or account and includes at least a timestamp and event type.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure of sensitive event content by sharing; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Alert metadata can link household activity across events
description: Even if payload content is minimized or protected, repeated transmission metadata on this flow (such as source/destination identifiers, timing, frequency, and device/account identifiers) can allow linking multiple motion events to the same household or user account over time.
assumptions: Network- or application-level identifiers remain stable enough across alerts to correlate events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via communication metadata; exact node id may vary.

title: Real-time alert transmission can identify a specific household or user
description: Identifiers or distinctive communication patterns in the alert flow may enable identification of the household, device, or account responsible for the motion event.
assumptions: The flow carries explicit identifiers, or the endpoint/network metadata is sufficiently distinctive to single out the sender.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from data in transit; exact node id may differ.

title: Backend storage and processing of motion alerts exposes behavioral patterns
description: On receipt, the mobile app backend may store, aggregate, or analyze motion alerts, enabling inference of residents' daily routines, absences, sleep patterns, or other sensitive behavioral information beyond the immediate notification purpose.
assumptions: The backend retains alerts or derived analytics rather than using them ephemerally only for delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure arising from recipient-side storage/analysis; exact node id may differ.

title: Secondary use of motion alerts beyond notification purpose
description: The backend could use received motion alerts for purposes not expected by residents, such as analytics, service improvement, profiling, or sharing with affiliates, making the processing of the alert data insufficiently transparent or unexpected.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and user expectations are not strictly enforced or communicated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness/non-transparent secondary use; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Backend processing of motion alerts may exceed consent or legal basis
description: If residents have not validly consented to, or are not otherwise informed of, backend receipt and retention of real-time motion alerts, the processing may be non-compliant with applicable privacy requirements.
assumptions: A consent, contract, or other legal basis is required for this processing and may be absent, invalid, or too broad.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance due to inadequate legal basis/notice; exact node id may differ.

title: Notification content discloses occupancy/activity information
description: By sending a motion-detected notification, the backend discloses personal information about activity at the homeowner's property, such as presence, movement patterns, or possible absence/presence at home.
assumptions: The notification contains or implies that motion was detected at a specific home associated with the homeowner.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure of personal data by sharing it with a recipient; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Push-notification metadata can link homeowner to device/home events
description: Metadata on the notification flow, such as device token, account identifier, timing, and repeated event patterns, may allow linking multiple motion events to the same homeowner, household, or device over time even if payload visibility is limited.
assumptions: Push delivery involves stable identifiers or observable metadata across repeated notifications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via communication metadata; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Notification metadata may identify the homeowner or household
description: Identifiers used to route the push notification, or the combination of timing and service metadata, may enable identification of the homeowner, their device, or their residence.
assumptions: The push channel exposes stable routing identifiers or other identifying metadata to intermediaries or observers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from data-flow metadata; exact node id may differ.

title: Notification content may be exposed in transit or on lock screen
description: The motion alert payload may reveal sensitive household activity if exposed during transmission through notification infrastructure or displayed on the phone lock screen where others can see it.
assumptions: Notification text is not fully minimized and may be visible to intermediaries or nearby people via previews.
uncertainty_note: This combines in-transit and delivery/display disclosure concerns; exact tree node may be more specific in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Unexpected or overly detailed notification use may exceed homeowner expectations
description: If the homeowner receives highly detailed motion notifications or notifications at a frequency/granularity they did not expect, the processing may be unaware or surprising, reducing transparency about how event data is used in alerts.
assumptions: Users may not fully understand notification granularity, preview behavior, or when alerts are generated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency at the recipient side; exact node id may differ.

title: Notifications may be sent without valid or sufficiently specific consent/preferences
description: The backend may push motion-detected alerts even when the homeowner has not clearly consented to this notification type, channel, timing, or content detail, creating a non-compliance risk with consent and preference requirements.
assumptions: Notification preferences or consent management may be absent, outdated, or insufficiently granular.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for consent/compliance issues; exact node id may differ.

title: Shared aggregated analytics may still enable linkage across datasets
description: Even if the backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics, the aggregation dimensions, cohort definitions, timestamps, app version, region, or device-class breakdowns may allow the vendor to link records or reports with other datasets it already holds, enabling correlation of the same user groups or devices over time.
assumptions: Assumes the shared analytics include repeated reports, stable cohort keys, fine-grained dimensions, or metadata that can be correlated by the vendor.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro linkage subtree numbering may vary.

title: Aggregated analytics may still permit inference of individual or group identity
description: If aggregates are too granular or based on small cohorts, the recipient may infer the presence, behavior, or identity of particular users or devices, especially when combined with auxiliary information.
assumptions: Assumes some analytics slices may have low cardinality or unique combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability via insufficient aggregation / singling out.

title: Shared usage analytics may disclose sensitive behavior patterns
description: Device-usage analytics can reveal behavioral patterns such as feature usage, activity times, geography, or engagement trends. Even in aggregated form, these disclosures may expose sensitive information about users or small groups.
assumptions: Assumes analytics include dimensions or segments from which sensitive habits, locations, or interests can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that backend shares analytics with a third-party vendor
description: If the app's notices do not clearly explain that aggregated device-usage analytics are sent to an external analytics vendor, users may lack awareness of this downstream processing.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-app disclosures are incomplete, unclear, or not presented contextually.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node id.

title: Sharing analytics with vendor may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: The backend may disclose analytics to the cloud analytics vendor without a valid legal basis, outside the scope of user consent, or beyond the purposes stated in the privacy notice, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes applicable law or policy requires transparency, purpose limitation, consent, contract controls, or another legal basis for third-party analytics sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Transmission metadata may enable linkage
description: Even if payload contents are aggregated, data-flow metadata such as endpoint identities, timing, frequency, volume, and recurring transfer patterns may allow linkage of analytics batches to specific campaigns, releases, incidents, or user populations.
assumptions: Assumes an observer or intermediary can access network metadata or transfer characteristics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit flow-centric linkage node id.

title: Analytics data in transit could be exposed
description: If the transfer to the cloud analytics vendor is insufficiently protected, aggregated analytics and associated metadata could be intercepted or exposed during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes transport security, endpoint authentication, or routing protections may be weak or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure-in-transit node id.

title: Vendor may link received analytics with other customer or third-party datasets
description: Upon receipt, the cloud analytics vendor may correlate the shared analytics with its own telemetry, advertising, or other customer datasets, increasing the ability to link cohorts, applications, or potentially individuals across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor has access to additional datasets and contractual/technical controls do not fully prevent cross-context correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit destination-side linkage node id.

title: Vendor may re-identify individuals from aggregated analytics
description: The vendor may use auxiliary data, historical reports, or small-cell analysis to infer the identity or presence of specific users or devices from ostensibly aggregated analytics.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor has sufficient side information or receives repeated granular aggregates over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit destination-side identifiability node id.

title: Vendor processing may disclose information beyond intended analytics purpose
description: The vendor may store, analyze, or share the received analytics in ways that reveal sensitive business or user-behavior information beyond the original purpose of service analytics.
assumptions: Assumes vendor retention, internal access, onward sharing, or secondary use are not tightly constrained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit destination-side disclosure node id.

title: Users may be unaware of vendor-side retention and secondary use
description: Users may not understand how long the vendor retains the analytics, whether it combines them with other data, or whether it uses them for service improvement or other secondary purposes.
assumptions: Assumes vendor practices are not fully disclosed to users by the app provider.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit destination-side unawareness node id.

title: Vendor-side processing may violate contractual or regulatory constraints
description: The vendor's receipt, retention, cross-border transfer, or secondary use of the analytics may conflict with data-processing agreements, purpose limitation, minimization requirements, or other privacy obligations.
assumptions: Assumes applicable contractual, regulatory, or policy constraints govern third-party analytics processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit destination-side non-compliance node id.

title: Linkability via repeated video-retrieval metadata
description: Metadata on this retrieval flow (e.g., clip identifier, camera/device identifier, homeowner account/session identifier, timestamps, IP/network information, and retrieval frequency) could allow an observer or intermediary to correlate multiple playback events to the same household, device, or user over time.
assumptions: Assumes flow metadata is observable in logs, monitoring systems, or by network intermediaries beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability from observable communication metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Identifiability of homeowner from retrieval metadata
description: Even if the video payload is protected, metadata on the transfer may reveal or strongly suggest the identity of the homeowner or household, for example through stable account references, camera IDs, IP addresses, or location-associated network endpoints.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers or quasi-identifiers are present in requests, headers, URLs, or transport/log metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability caused by data-in-transit metadata.

title: Disclosure of sensitive video content in transit
description: The retrieved clip may contain highly sensitive personal data about residents, visitors, routines, possessions, or activities. If the flow is intercepted, misrouted, insufficiently encrypted, or exposed through verbose logging/caching, the video content could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection, endpoint authentication, logging, and caching controls may be imperfect or bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for confidentiality/disclosure of content during transfer.

title: Over-disclosure by cloud storage when serving the clip
description: Cloud Video Storage may return more data than necessary for playback, such as extra footage before/after the requested interval, embedded metadata, thumbnails, audio tracks, or related clips, thereby disclosing additional personal information to the backend.
assumptions: Assumes retrieval APIs or object layouts may include bundled metadata or broader time ranges than minimally required.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for source-side over-disclosure; exact subnode may differ.

title: Disclosure through backend logging, caching, or secondary use
description: Upon receiving the clip, the Mobile App Backend may store temporary copies, generate thumbnails/transcodes, log object references, or expose the clip to internal services, increasing the chance that sensitive video or associated metadata is disclosed beyond the immediate playback purpose.
assumptions: Assumes backend performs operational logging, caching, analytics, debugging, or media processing.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for destination-side disclosure due to recipient processing/storage.

title: Unawareness of backend-side processing of retrieved video
description: The homeowner may be unaware that, when a clip is retrieved for playback, the backend could cache it, analyze it, retain access logs, or share it with supporting services. This reduces transparency about how playback requests affect personal data processing.
assumptions: Assumes notices do not clearly explain backend retrieval, caching, retention, and onward processing practices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/unawareness; exact subnode may vary.

title: Playback retrieval incompatible with original collection purpose
description: Video originally collected for home security/event recording may be further processed by the backend for analytics, service improvement, model training, or troubleshooting when retrieved, which may be incompatible with the user's expected playback purpose.
assumptions: Assumes backend or connected services may repurpose retrieved clips or metadata beyond delivering playback.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for non-compliance/purpose incompatibility at the destination.
